sections.Overview:
Costco Wholesale Corporation operates membership warehouses and e-commerce platforms across multiple countries, primarily in the United States, Puerto Rico, Canada, Mexico, Japan, and several other markets worldwide. Its business model emphasizes offering a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products at low prices, leveraging high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover to achieve operating efficiencies. Memberships provide recurring revenue through annual fees, and Executive memberships yield additional rewards driving sales. The company's warehouses are large, no-frills facilities designed for efficient inventory management and self-service shopping, bolstered by ancillary services such as gasoline stations and pharmacies that complement the core warehouse business [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, lines L000733-L000765].

Insight: Costco's growth outlook is dependent on successfully acquiring suitable sites for new warehouses amidst increasing local regulatory and community challenges, which pose notable execution risk to expansion and comparable sales, as explicitly stated by management in their risk disclosures [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, line L000839] [C:1].
sections.Market Positioning and Growth Outlook: Costco positions itself competitively by combining low prices with high-quality merchandise, focusing on fast-selling product models with relatively low SKU counts per warehouse compared to other broadline retailers, which supports improved inventory turnover and cost control. The membership warehouse format creates customer loyalty and consistent renewal rates (92.3% in the U.S. and Canada, 89.8% worldwide). The company's geographic diversification covers mature and growth markets with ongoing warehouse expansion. It also benefits from a direct-sourcing supply chain that reduces dependency on single suppliers and leverages private-label goods to enhance value [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, lines L000737-L000768, L000773-L000784; EX-99.1 accession 0000909832-26-000084, lines L000021]. The increase in net sales and comparable sales across all regions, including digitally enabled sales rising 20.9% for the fiscal year, signals growth momentum [EX-99.1 lines L000010-L000018].

sections.Future Developments and Strategic Recomm: Costco's expansion strategy involves opening new warehouses in existing and new markets, although it acknowledges risks such as competition for locations, community opposition, and regulation that may impact growth. It aims to maintain and grow membership populations, particularly Executive members, to sustain sales penetration. Strategic focus should continue on supply chain diversification, further development of e-commerce, and enhancement of ancillary services to increase shopping frequency. Monitoring penetration and renewal rates, especially in newer geographies, and responding to competitive pressures with efficiency improvements and member benefits will be critical. Attention to market-specific risks, such as heavier dependence on the U.S. and specifically California operations, needs to be balanced by geographic expansion and supply chain resilience [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, lines L000838-L000841; L000773-L000784; EX-99.1 accession 0000909832-26-000084, lines L000010-L000021].
sections.Investment Recommendation:
Hold (provisional): The deciding figure is Costco's operating margin at 3.85% for fiscal 2026 [C:M1], which is below peers Walmart (4.18%) and Target (4.88%) despite solid revenue growth of 10.14% [C:G1]. This suggests positive growth momentum but margin pressure and risks on expansion execution create uncertainty.

COSTCO WHOLESALE CORPORATION REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FISCAL YEAR 2026 OPERATING RESULTS
ISSAQUAH, Wash., September 24, 2026 - Costco Wholesale Corporation (“Costco” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: COST) today announced its operating results for the 16-week fourth quarter and the 52-week fiscal year ended August 30, 2026.
Net sales for the quarter increased 11.2 percent, to $93.9 billion, from $84.4 billion last year. Net sales for the fiscal year increased 10.1 percent, to $297.2 billion, from $269.9 billion last year.
Comparable sales for the fourth quarter and fiscal year were as follows:
| 16 Weeks |  | 16 Weeks |  | 52 Weeks |  | 52 Weeks
|  |  | Adjusted* |  |  |  | Adjusted*
U.S. | 10.7% |  | 7.2% |  | 8.2% |  | 6.6%
Canada | 5.0% |  | 4.6% |  | 7.8% |  | 6.7%
Other International | 7.0% |  | 6.2% |  | 9.8% |  | 6.5%
Total Company | 9.4% |  | 6.7% |  | 8.4% |  | 6.6%
Digitally-Enabled | 19.5% |  | 19.8% |  | 20.9% |  | 20.7%
*Excluding the impacts from changes in gasoline prices and foreign exchange.
Net income for the fourth quarter was $2.998 billion, $6.75 per diluted share, compared to $2.610 billion, $5.87 per diluted share, last year. This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values. Net income for the fiscal year was $9.226 billion, $20.76 per diluted share, compared to $8.099 billion, $18.21 per diluted share, last year.
Costco currently operates 939 warehouses, including 647 in the United States and Puerto Rico, 115 in Canada, 43 in Mexico, 37 in Japan, 29 in the United Kingdom, 20 in Korea, 15 in Australia, 14 in Taiwan, seven in China, five in Spain, three in France, two in Sweden, and one each in Iceland, and New Zealand. Costco also operates e-commerce sites in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Mexico, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Australia, and China.
A conference call to discuss these results is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. (PT) today, September 24, 2026, and will be available via a webcast on investor.costco.com (click “Events & Presentations”).
